STEP 1 - Scene: A small meal of broccoli florets and a whole pear (or similar green-yellow fruit) on a white square plate, photographed from directly above.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white plate is roughly square, about 24 cm across its width. Area ≈ 24 × 24 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 490 cm². Using a circular approximation for a 24 cm plate: 3.14 × 12² ≈ 452 cm². I'll use ~470 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Broccoli florets (cluster of about 4 larger florets plus one small floret)
- Whole pear (green-yellow, roughly 8 cm diameter)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Broccoli: spans roughly 9 × 8 cm of plate, about 12% of vessel area (~55 cm²)
- Pear: about 8 cm diameter, ~50 cm² footprint, ~11% of vessel area

Food covers about 23% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Broccoli: 55 cm² × ~5 cm height (outer envelope of the florets) ≈ 275 ml
- Pear: a roughly ellipsoidal fruit, about 8 cm × 7 cm × 7 cm ≈ 0.52 × 8 × 7 × 7 ≈ 200 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Broccoli: 275 ml × 0.5 g/ml ≈ 140 g. Individual florets are quite airy, so I'll take ~120 g as a sensible figure for the visible pile.
- Pear: whole fruit is a dense solid; ~200 ml × 0.85 ≈ 170 g. Pear weight is typically ~150–180 g for a fruit this size; I'll use 165 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Broccoli, raw/cooked-equivalent: ~34 kcal/100 g → 120 g × 0.34 ≈ 41 kcal
- Pear, raw: ~57 kcal/100 g → 165 g × 0.57 ≈ 94 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A small amount of broccoli plus one whole pear on a large plate is plausible at about 285 g total and ~135 kcal. The plate is only partly covered, so the total is modest, which fits the visible content.
